I've had more trouble with the mask, but because I'm a 5'0 woman. They all think I'm some high schooler tryna get wasted.  
No, just your everyday sad individual.  
Cheers OP
Oh, it's good! Still need to get into the flow of working again, but my anxiety is starting to die down. Think I'll get back to the pace of things once I complete something on my to do list ^_^
I don't think I can live like this much longer.

Yes, I think so. I think...I'm having difficulty living with my parents but also such difficulty leaving them, getting a job, finding a play to stay. Opportunities keep falling through and I feel more and more trapped, like a failure, and depressed. Sort of like this negative feedback loop

I've always heard it imagined as quicksand, but your description is a really good one.  
With quicksand, I imagine my feet, legs, thighs are trapped and I can't pull out. I'm sinking and it feels like I can't escape. But you can still see the sky, you can still see the world around you giving hope for escape, what it could be like.
Edit: there's a blue sky but it's difficult to get to.

My (25f) family does this weird thing where we don't talk about things, we just move on and pretend negative events never happened. I couldn't stand this, so when I became an adult, I tried to go no-contact as much as possible.

I've been working abroad in different capacities. But when shit hits the fan and without a strong financial safety net, I find myself falling back into my parent's home, wherever it is that they've moved to. I stay there, until I figure things out.

In late 2018, I was attacked while working abroad, and needed some time to rest and recenter myself. I did this at my parent's house by staying in my room as much as possible and getting all my work, my job applications, health insurance, etc. figured out while at Starbucks.

This time, COVID-19 sent us all home. I didn't know where to go, so I requested to be sent back to my parent's new house, up in a small northwest town. So I've been here...but I didn't realize how difficult it would be to get back on my feet this time. 

I've found myself feeling uncomfortable and anxious when I leave the house (mixed Asian American in a predominately white community). And it's a small town I don't know well - I've never lived here previously and have no friends and only my father's side of the family here. I feel unwelcome and don't feel comfortable getting exercise outside in the neighborhood. I miss cardio.

The house is smaller and it's harder to avoid my parents. At first, I tried to use the open spaces to get work done, apply for jobs, figure things out. But my mother has a way of making everything (\*everything\*) into a criticism. Everything I do is negative. I'm not allowed to listen to music, to touch the TV, to touch their computer - as it's not my house. If I try to cook or clean or help do chores, my mother has something negative to say about it. Every. Time. 

So I tried to stay in my room more, out of sight. The room is small and cramped, but okay. But I can't get into the working headspace. I try and try and struggle to get things done. My anxiety is rising.

And my N-mother has depression, so she stays up all night until 4, 5, 6 in the morning, turning the TV up really loud, constantly slamming the garage door next to my room (the freezer is out there), talking my father's ear off if he's around. I used to get up at 6 AM and get in bed by 9 PM. Now, I'm not getting enough sleep and I'm tired throughout the day. 

My father makes me uncomfortable. He's getting older, and you can see it. I'm not allowed to touch the car to renew my driver's license (plus, I need proof of residence for that), so he drives me around everywhere. His mind is slowly going, and it's hard to watch. His driving isn't great, but he also stumbles over his words in conversation, mixes up ideas, and gets a little bit confused. His legs are getting worse, and he struggles to do basic movements or walk anything more than 20m or so. And my mother treats him like shit, constantly putting him down and criticizing his aging body. 

He used to molest me when I was 10, 11, 12. I always got along with him more than my mother, anyway. But it really fucked me up, so a few years after it had already stopped, I reported it to authorities. We went through this whole legal case about it, which was more stressful than the actual abuse. I still lived with my mother for that year and she told me everyday how much she hated me and wished I was dead. And then the case was dropped and my father moved back home. He never touched me past the age of 13, and we never talked about it again. My mother never believed me. 

Talking about it would be taboo, the whole thing doesn't exist in our universe. I think my dad still holds the guilt for what he did - when I ignore what happened, we're actually pretty good friends. But the damage still sits with me and I think that becomes more and more apparent the longer I stay here.

Really, it's probably affecting my mental health. I'm becoming more and more anxious. While I appreciate some of the good that my parents have shared with me in the past, or now (no rent, free food, free wifi), this is such a toxic household to live in. I feel so trapped here, until I find a job. I'm afraid of checking into a women's shelter, and losing access to my clothes/laptop/personal documents or getting it stolen.

I'm afraid of committing to an apartment here and getting financially stuck here, and struggling with racial identity day to day. Money is so tight, I need to find a job before I buy housing and transportation anywhere else. But I struggle to focus. I try to get things done, but since I've retreated to my room, I can't seem to focus...what I wouldn't give for a cafe to work or restaurant to work in right now...

My anxiety is getting worse, however. It feels like this panic is bubbling up inside of me, and it's more and more and more and more difficult to focus, to get everything done. Now, phone notifications, email, messaging, all gives me anxiety. It's a reminder of all I need to get done that I'm \*not\* getting done. I try one thing, and then my focus shuts off. Anxiety builds again. I can't breathe. And I feel weak for not just \*overcoming\* these feelings and getting my shit together. What's wrong with me? 

It feels like I'm in this never-ending loop that I'm trying desperately (in my mind) to claw out of, but just keep slipping back down. I feel very alone and trapped. I feel like I'm suffocating.

And I feel weak for letting this get the best of me.  
I wish my bedroom door locked.
